verses.english: Linked Discourses 4.16
2. Rule
The Alms Bowls
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ upādāya bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
verses.english: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk on the topic of the five grasping aggregates.

verses.pali: Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
verses.english: And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.
Then Māra thought,

verses.pali: “ayaṁ kho samaṇo gotamo pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ upādāya bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti.
verses.english: “This ascetic Gotama is educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk on the topic of the five grasping aggregates.

verses.pali: Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
verses.english: And the mendicants are paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

verses.pali: Yannūnāhaṁ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṁ vicakkhukammāyā”ti.
verses.english: Why don’t I go and pull the wool over their eyes?”

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā pattā abbhokāse nikkhittā honti.
verses.english: At that time several alms bowls were placed in the open air.

verses.pali: Atha kho māro pāpimā balībaddavaṇṇaṁ abhinimminitvā yena te pattā tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then Māra the Wicked manifested in the form of an ox and approached those bowls.

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: One of the mendicants said to another,
“Mendicant, mendicant, that ox will break the bowls.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When this was said, the Buddha said to that mendicant,
“Mendicant, that’s no ox.

verses.pali: Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṁ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti.
verses.english: That’s Māra the Wicked come to pull the wool over your eyes!”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṁ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṁ pāpimantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha, knowing that this was Māra the Wicked, addressed him in verse:
“Form, what is felt, and perception,
consciousness, and what is chosen:
‘I am not this’ and ‘this is not mine’;
that’s how to be free of desire for them.
When you’re detached, secure,
all fetters transcended,
though Māra and his army chase everywhere
they never find you.”
Then Māra … vanished right there.
